title: Larry and the boy at the French fort, Nui Ba Den
description: Larry (left), looking down — probably at reports, he says — stands among the granite boulders of the French fort on Núi Bà Đen beside a smiling boy in an oversized field jacket. The boy, about twelve, had been shot in the leg, was married at ten, and had two children; "The kid was with me all the time". Painted inscriptions cover the rock face; a doorway is built into the mortared stone. Larry's radio was outside, and about five Air Force men, he remembers, were putting in something he describes with a question mark as a radar, with a search antenna that rotated, built up in the boulders.
researchNotes: Larry's own account (Memories comment, 2026-08-15; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0009-c18032407.json). His comment names the French fort, not the mountain; the fort is placed on Núi Bà Đen by his own hand (FORT on the NUI BA DEN sheet, VD-0002) and by his 2026-09-03 words at VN-0044 about the boy who was with him on the mountain. The vision survey had proposed the same place; that is not what the location rests on. VN-0059 shows the same corner from behind — Larry points to the walkway where the two of them stood — plus his radio area. The Air Force radar installation is a potentially documentable event (a USAF radar site on Núi Bà Đen would appear in Air Force records) that could date this frame. The boy's name is not recalled; asked twice (2026-08-15, 2026-09-03), it is treated as a settled negative. The painted inscriptions remain magnification targets.
